# action.docker_node_activate

<!-- Code generated by tools/genskill from the provider schema. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Kind: action. Back to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

Sets a swarm node's availability back to `active`, like `docker node update --availability active`. The scheduler can then place new tasks on it; running services are not rebalanced. The provider's host must be a swarm manager.

Actions need Terraform >= 1.14. They keep no state: they run when a
resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { ... } }` fires, or on demand with
`terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_node_activate.<name>`. Arguments go inside
the action's `config` block.

## Usage

```terraform
action "docker_node_activate" "<name>" {
  config {
    # arguments below
  }
}

# Run it: lifecycle { action_trigger { events = [after_create] actions = [action.docker_node_activate.<name>] } }
# on a resource, or: terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_node_activate.<name>
```

## Arguments and attributes

| Name | Type | Status | Forces replacement | Sensitive | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node` | `string` | required |  |  | Node ID, hostname or node name. |

## Example

```terraform
variable "node" {
  type    = string
  default = "worker-1"
}

resource "terraform_data" "back_in_service" {
  input = var.node

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.docker_node_activate.back]
    }
  }
}

# Makes a drained node schedulable again. On demand:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_node_activate.back
action "docker_node_activate" "back" {
  config {
    node = var.node
  }
}
```
